quotes.text: Co-pilot doesn't create new access. It removes the effort needed to use the access you already gave people.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Captures the core insight that Copilot exposes existing permission problems rather than creating new ones.

quotes.text: You didn't have good governance, you had friction posing as protection, and it lasted because most people never had the time or patience to test the edges of their own access.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Names the hidden security-through-obscurity model that AI retrieval breaks.

quotes.text: In a copilot environment labels need to become decision signals. They have to tell downstream controls what content can be processed, what should be blocked, and where stricter rules should apply.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes sensitivity labels from passive stickers into active enforcement signals.

quotes.text: If you can't map your sensitive data or verify who has access to it, you aren't actually scaling AI in a meaningful way. You are simply scaling uncertainty
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A clear warning against scaling Copilot before establishing a data baseline.

quotes.text: AI governance fails when teams confuse policy intent with policy reality. The setting might exist, but the estate hasn't caught up yet.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Concise reminder that published policies need verification before teams rely on them.

chapters.title: Purview: build the perimeter around context

takeaways: Copilot does not create new access; it removes the friction that used to hide overshared content, so permission hygiene must come before scale.
Microsoft Purview works best label-first: sensitivity labels, adaptive scopes and prompt-level DLP let policy follow the meaning of content instead of its location.
Audit data closes the loop, letting teams prove safe usage, investigate incidents and tune policies as Copilot usage patterns change.
hook: Copilot does not break your permissions, it simply makes every overshared file instantly findable. This episode is for IT, security and compliance leaders planning or stuck in a Copilot rollout, and it shows how a Microsoft Purview baseline of labels, adaptive scopes, prompt-level DLP and audit turns that exposure into controlled adoption.
